definition: Coal, oil or natural gas: a fuel formed over millions of years from the remains of plants and animals, holding energy in a chemical store and non-renewable.
An energy resource that is replaced naturally as fast as we use it, so it will not run out, such as wind, tides, sunlight or biofuels.
An energy resource that is used up much faster than it forms, so it will run out, such as fossil fuels and nuclear fuel.
A machine, turned by a turbine or engine, that uses electromagnetic induction to produce an electric current, transferring energy from its kinetic store by electrical work.
The fraction of the total energy (or power) input that a device transfers usefully, often given as a percentage; it can never be more than 100%.
The joining of small nuclei, such as hydrogen, to form a larger nucleus, releasing energy; it is how the Sun releases its energy.
